name: twoSidedSubst_firstColsCoord
summary: Commute the substitution past inFirstCols (it becomes a row substitution by cᵀ on the first columns and the substitution c, g on the coefficients), and move the row substitution across the Fock pairing, where it becomes the Schur matrix.

steps.claim: Record the behaviour of the Fock pairing under the coefficientwise algebra map twoSidedSubst c g (map_fockPairing, applied to inFirstCols F'), and apply firstColsCoord κ (·) l to both sides of H: the coordinate of twoSidedSubst c (diag(1, g)) F' equals that of s·F.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨_, H⟩ :=
    map_fockPairing (twoSidedSubst c g).1 (inFirstCols F'), congr(firstColsCoord κ $H l)

steps.claim: In that equation, inFirstCols ∘ twoSidedSubst c (diag(1, g)) = (row substitution by c_τᵀ on the first columns) ∘ (twoSidedSubst c g on the coefficients) ∘ inFirstCols, as ℂ-algebra maps (they agree on every variable: algHom_ext).
steps.lean:
rw [firstColsCoord, comp_aeval_apply, (MvPolynomial.algHom_ext (by simp [inFirstCols, rowSubst,
    ← C_mul']) : aeval _ = ((rowSubst fun τ ↦ ((c τ).map C)ᵀ).restrictScalars ℂ).comp
    ((mapAlgHom (twoSidedSubst c g)).comp inFirstCols))] at H

steps.claim: Moving the row substitution across the Fock pairing (fockPairing_rowSubst: it becomes the transposed substitution on the basis polynomial, whose expansion in the basis is the Schur matrix, schur_map) and collecting the scalars gives Σ_{l'} S_κ(c)_{l l'}·(substituted coordinate of F' at l') = s·firstColsCoord κ F l.
steps.lean: simp_all [fockPairing_rowSubst, schur_map, C_mul', firstColsCoord, smul_comm _ _⁻¹, smul_sum]
